title: Buying a non-current asset

match.reason: The closest bank point covers recording an asset at cost, but it does not teach the loan side of the brief, which adds a liability repaid over time, so that is a new step and no bank point matches the whole idea.

draft.title: Buying a non-current asset
card: A non-current asset is something a business owns and expects to use for more than one year, such as a van or a machine.
It is recorded at cost. Cost is the price paid plus any amount needed to get the asset ready for use, such as delivery and installation.
the asset account is debited and the bank account is credited. Total assets stay the same, because one asset rises and another falls.
the asset account is debited at cost and a loan account is credited. The loan is a liability, and each repayment reduces it over time.
draft.remember: Record the asset at cost. Cash lowers the bank account, while a loan adds a liability.

a.q: Ravi's Bakery in Ballarat buys an oven for $9,000 cash. How is the purchase recorded?
opts: Debit Oven, credit Bank
Debit Bank, credit Oven
Debit Oven, credit Loan
Debit Expense, credit Bank
a.why: The oven is an asset the bakery will use for years, so the asset account is debited at cost. Cash leaves the bank account, so it is credited. An expense entry is wrong because the oven will be used for more than one year.
a.clue: The oven comes in and cash goes out.

b.q: Tess's Landscaping in Geelong buys a trailer for $12,000 using a bank loan. What is the effect of the purchase?
opts: Assets and liabilities both rise by $12,000
Assets rise by $12,000 and liabilities stay the same
Assets fall by $12,000 and liabilities rise
Assets and liabilities both stay the same
b.why: The trailer is recorded at cost, so assets rise by $12,000. The loan is owed to the bank, so liabilities rise by $12,000 too. Liabilities do not stay the same, because no cash was paid out to cancel the debt.
b.clue: Ask who is owed the money after the purchase.

b.best: Assets and liabilities both rise by $12,000

problems.detail: The why's last sentence gives a muddled reason: liabilities rise because a new loan is owed to the bank, not because 'no cash was paid out to cancel the debt'. This could confuse students about why the liability changes.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and the card is accurate. The only issue is a confusing final sentence in the explanation for question b.
